description:
Deep Relaxation Music | Santoor Instrumental | 1.5 Hours

This is for the end of the day when your body still hasn't gotten the message that it's over.

Ninety minutes of slow, meditative santoor in Raga Yaman — an evening raga with an open, expansive quality that gently unties what the day wound tight. No rush. No peak. Just a long, unhurried descent into stillness.

What you'll hear: the hammered shimmer of santoor with long phrase spaces, soft tanpura drone underneath, tuned to 432Hz with alpha wave support for physical release.

Best for: after work · unwinding before bed · body scan or progressive relaxation · sitting with a quiet cup of tea when you need the room to finally go still.

🔔 Subscribe to Raga Focus for Indian instrumental music that helps you actually relax.
thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate warm-gold patterned border, aged parchment background. EVENING/DUSK palette — deep warm amber and soft teal, candlelight glow, still and unhurried. Central composition: a pair of santoor mallets resting on the strings of a santoor — no hands, no figure — as if the player has just stopped and the room has gone quiet. One candle glowing softly in the background. The instrument fills most of the frame. Overlay text 'DEEP RELAXATION' in large bold teal serif, top or center. Mobile-first: text must read in under 1 second. The candlelight + resting mallets = permission to stop. Miniature-art border gives cultural authenticity. Clean, uncluttered composition.
suno_prompt_A: Indian classical instrumental, Raga Yaman — raised 4th (teevra Ma), expansive outward open evening character, gradually settling and releasing, hammered santoor dulcimer with characteristic bright percussive attack and long warm resonant sustain, slow deliberate mallet strikes with generous space between phrases — like the body finally getting permission to put down the weight it has been carrying, soft tanpura drone underneath holding everything still, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, slow tempo 55-60 BPM, mid-low register with occasional bright peaks, warm golden reverb, seamless loop-friendly ambient texture, no vocals, no humming, no human voice
suno_prompt_B: Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming, Indian classical santoor deep relaxation, Raga Yaman — raised 4th, expansive evening open quality, hammered santoor dulcimer slow deliberate mallet strikes with long resonant sustain and generous space between phrases, soft tanpura drone, no tabla, 432Hz, 55-60 BPM, mid-low warm register, golden reverb, seamless loop, like the body finally releasing what the day wound tight

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: SLOW and SPACIOUS is the goal — reference the Stress Relief Santoor 3hr (TXfk2UU5MjI, 50:15 AVD) for pacing. Long phrase pauses are a feature not a bug. No tabla. Yaman = evening open quality, should feel like a room going quiet after a long day. If a clip sounds busy or rushed, regenerate. Opening should be the calmest, most inviting phrase — no abrupt attack at the start.
